Name: Big Bull Creek Park
Description: Big Bull Creek Park's splash pad is located at the Sunflower Road access north of 207th Street as part of a nature play area. The splash pad operates seasonally from after Memorial Day through October 15 and is activated by tapping a blue dot on the pavement. The surrounding area includes a three-quarter-mile paved trail, picnic shelters, restroom facilities, and parking, with connections to nearby Martin Creek Park in Edgerton.

Name: Lincoln Park (Coach Eddie Shannon Park)
Description: This 17-acre Palmetto park includes a free splash pad featuring interactive water play structures, open seasonally with attendants on duty throughout operating hours. The splash pad sits within a larger recreational complex that offers playgrounds, basketball courts, soccer and football fields, along with amenities including restrooms, shade structures, picnic areas, grills, and parking. Children under 13 must be supervised by an adult; the facility may close during inclement weather, heavy rain, or lightning. The park also contains a pool with slides and lap area, walking trails, and a StoryWalk program along the football field perimeter.

Description: South Beach Park's seasonal splash pad is located at Osceola Avenue and South Beach Parkway in Jacksonville Beach and operates daily from 7 AM to 8 PM at no cost. The facility is part of a larger park that includes a children's playground, picnic shelters with grills available for reservation, restrooms, shade structures, parking, and changing rooms. The splash pad welcomes families and pairs well with the park's other recreational amenities.
Full Address: 2514 S Beach Pkwy, Jacksonville Beach, FL 32250

Name: SKYLAKE Adventures
Description: SKYLAKE Adventures is an outdoor water park in Sheridan, Indiana, opening June 4th with a mix of floating obstacle courses and water slides. Initial attractions include the X-Tower climbing feature, SKY Slides for racing, the Splash Challenge for adults, Tidal Trek designed for younger children, and three themed beach areas with varying water depths and sand. General admission starts at $55 for adults and $50 for children ages 4–9, with annual passes available. The facility provides parking, restrooms, onsite dining, and accessibility accommodations.

Name: Sugar Hollow Marina
Description: Sugar Hollow Water Park features an inflatable obstacle course setup on the water designed for visitors ages 7 and up (48 inches minimum height). The facility operates seasonally with extended hours on weekends, provides free admission, and requires all participants to wear U.S. Coast Guard-approved life jackets and sign a waiver before use. Parking, restrooms, and accessibility are available on-site, though there is no lifeguard on duty and swimmers use the course at their own risk.
Hours:
Monday: 10AM–4PM
Tuesday: 10AM–4PM
Wednesday: 10AM–4PM
Thursday: 10AM–4PM
Friday: 10AM–9PM
Saturday: 10AM–9PM
Sunday: 10AM–7PM

Name: Lazy L Lake Campground
Description: Lazy L Lake Campground features a floating inflatable obstacle course water park anchored on its 75-acre private lake, open daily from Memorial Day through Labor Day (weather permitting). The water park accommodates ages 6–60 with a minimum height of 4 feet, includes provided buoyancy vests, and welcomes day guests without requiring a campground reservation beyond the day-use fee. Located in West Terre Haute, the facility offers parking, restrooms, picnic areas, and is accessible to families and kids seeking water recreation alongside camping and other lake activities.
Address: 545 Lazy Lake Rd, West Terre Haute, IN 47885

Name: Mt. Olympus - Building 3,4,5
Description: Mt. Olympus Water & Theme Park operates year-round with indoor attractions and a seasonal outdoor water park (mid-May through mid-September). The facility features a 145-foot tall waterslide and Medusa's Slidewheel, a rotating waterslide available indoors throughout the year. Park admission is included with hotel stays at the property, and the venue offers rides and attractions designed for all ages.
Address: 1621 Wisconsin Dells Pkwy, Wisconsin Dells, WI 53965

Name: Jellystone Park� Caledonia
Description: Jellystone Park in Caledonia features multiple water attractions including an activity pool with underwater play elements, fast-paced water slides with height and weight restrictions, and Yogi Bear's Picnic Splash area with additional slides and a dumping bucket structure. The water zone operates seasonally from Memorial Day Weekend through Labor Day Weekend, with the activity pool remaining open into late September weather permitting. The facility includes an ADA-accessible activity pool lift, accessible restrooms, ample parking, and camping accommodations ranging from luxury cabins to RV and tent sites. Admission to the water features is complimentary for overnight guests, and the park offers numerous additional amenities including mini golf, a ropes course, playgrounds, and an action zone with inflatables.

Name: Jubilee Splash Pad
Description: Jubilee Splash Pad is a splash pad in Daphne, Alabama. Admission is free. On-site amenities include restrooms and shaded seating. It includes gentler water features suited to toddlers.

Name: Fairhopers Community Park
Description: Fairhopers Community Park is a splash pad in Fairhope, Alabama. Admission is free. On-site amenities include restrooms, picnic areas, shaded seating, and an adjacent playground. It is open daily. It includes gentler water features suited to toddlers.

Name: The Splash Pad at Plaza DeLuna
Description: The Splash Pad at Plaza DeLuna is a free water play area located on South Palafox Street in Pensacola, operating daily from mid-March through October, 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. The splash pad features a fountain and is equipped with a wind sensor that automatically shuts off water flow when winds exceed 10 mph to protect the facility's pump system. Visitors enjoy nearby amenities including parking, picnic areas, shade, and a snack bar at deLuna's Chat & Chew Grill (open 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily), plus restroom facilities and a scenic waterfront location at the end of Palafox Pier.
Hours: Daily mid-March through October from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m.

Name: The Children's Park at Town Square Las Vegas
Description: The Children's Park at Town Square features a splash park alongside a climbing cube, slides, and a trampoline, designed for children ages 10 and under. Operating daily from 10 a.m. to 8:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday, 10 a.m. to 9:30 p.m. Friday and Saturday, and 10 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. Sunday, the splash park closes seasonally on October 30th. Located adjacent to Town Square Park within the shopping and dining district, the venue offers free admission with restrooms, shade, parking, changing rooms, and a snack bar on-site.
Hours:
Monday- Thursday 10 a.m. to 8:30 p.m.
Friday & Saturday 10 a.m. to 9:30 p.m.
Sunday 10 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.

Name: Cole Park Splash Pad
Description: Cole Park Splash Pad is located at 2030 Ocean Dr along Corpus Christi Bay and features 23 interactive water jets and spray elements designed for young children. The facility includes shade structures and is fully accessible. Admission is free, and the splash pad operates seasonally from late May through early August. The venue sits within Cole Park, the city's premier waterfront park.

Name: Chehaw Park & Zoo
Description: Chehaw Park features a dedicated Splash Park designed for water play across all ages, operating seasonally from morning until dusk. The water attraction is one of the largest play parks in South Georgia and is included with general park admission, making it accessible to all visitors exploring this conservation-focused facility.

Name: South Cobb Aquatic Center
Description: South Cobb Aquatic Center is a year-round indoor facility with multiple pools designed for various swimming activities, including lap swimming and family recreation. The center features water slides and a dedicated spray area for children, along with diving boards. Programs include swim lessons for all ages and special services such as birthday party packages.

Name: Jones Park
Description: Jones Park features a splash pad as a primary water-play amenity, complemented by a playground module, amphitheater, and concrete walking paths. The facility includes dedicated infrastructure such as a splash pad pavilion and comfort station to support visitors. Additional amenities like outdoor fitness units and multiple rental pavilions make it a multipurpose community destination.

Name: East Roswell Sprayground
Description: East Roswell Sprayground offers free water play in a dedicated sprayground facility open seasonally during summer months. The venue provides interactive water features designed specifically for cooling off and recreation, with wheelchair-accessible facilities and amenities for visitors of all abilities.

Name: Fosco Park
Description: Fosco Park features an outdoor splash pad alongside interactive water play structures integrated into one of its two playgrounds, making water recreation a designed part of the park's offerings. The facility also includes an indoor Olympic-sized zero-depth pool, complementing the outdoor water attractions. Located on 6 acres in Chicago's Near West Side, the park combines aquatic amenities with courts, fields, and recreational programs for youth and adults.

Name: Andersen Center & Park
Description: Andersen Park features a splash pad among its primary recreational amenities, making it a destination for water play in Oak Park's northeast corner. The park also offers a playground, small soccer field, and outdoor fitness equipment, along with a recreation center that serves a variety of ages and interests.

Name: Maryknoll Park
Description: Maryknoll Splash Park is a water play area within Maryknoll Park in Glen Ellyn. The park district maintains this splash park as one of its primary recreational facilities, distinct from the broader park amenities like playgrounds and picnic areas. It serves as a seasonal destination for water-based recreation in the community.
Address: 845 Pershing Ave Unit 1, Glen Ellyn, IL 60137

Name: McKinley (William) Park
Description: McKinley Park features a dedicated water playground with multiple spray features and interactive elements designed for children to cool off during summer months. The facility also includes a shallow kiddie pool with a slide, providing additional water-play options. Water playgrounds operate seasonally from late June through late August.

Name: 31st Street Harbor
Description: This harbor features a recently renovated playground equipped with water features for children, plus a dedicated leisure pool open seasonally with public day passes and annual memberships available. The pool operates Wednesday through Sunday during summer months and welcomes visitors with affordable daily and seasonal pricing options.
Address: 3155 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60616

Name: Central Park of Maple Grove
Description: Central Park features a seasonal interactive fountain plaza spanning 2,100 square feet with 67 spray jets and arches designed for active water play. The fountain uses a filtered recycling system similar to a swimming pool and transforms with LED lighting effects at dusk. Children and visitors can play freely during posted hours with adult supervision required; swim diapers are mandatory for non-toilet-trained users.
Address: 12000 Central Park Way, Maple Grove, MN 55369

Name: Lake Los Angeles Parks & Conservation Association at Sorensen Community Regional Park
Description: Sorensen Community Regional Park features a dedicated splash pad alongside traditional play areas, sports facilities, and picnic amenities. The park serves as a multi-purpose community recreation venue with water play as one of its primary attractions for families and visitors.
Address: Park Association At Sorensen Regional & Community Park, 16801 E Ave P, Lake Los Angeles, CA 93591

Name: Gloria Molina Grand Park
Description: This downtown Los Angeles park features a wade-able pool and splash pad, making it a destination for water play alongside its broader appeal as a cultural gathering space. The 12-acre venue offers open daily access for families seeking casual water activities, picnics, and recreation near major arts institutions.
Address: 200 N Grand Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90012

Name: Annenberg Community Beach House
Description: This Santa Monica community destination features a splash pad alongside a historic swimming pool, playground, and beach sports courts. Set in a restored Gold Coast-era guest house with ocean views, the venue combines water play with cultural events, dining, and recreational activities for visitors of all ages.
Address: 415 Pacific Coast Hwy, Santa Monica, CA 90402

Name: Warner Park Pool & Splash Pad
Description: Warner Park Pool includes a dedicated splash pad with multiple interactive water features designed for recreational play, including jets that squirt, spray, and rain down on visitors. The facility offers a distinct water-play area separate from its swimming pools, with affordable day-use admission and seasonal programming for all ages.

Name: Centennial Center Park
Description: This 11-acre city park includes a dedicated splash pad equipped with a recirculating filtration system that continuously cleans and recycles water from a 4,000-gallon reservoir. The water feature is designed for children's play and is integrated into a larger park that offers picnic areas, walking paths, and educational exhibits about local history and the Cherry Creek Watershed.

Name: Gregory Mill Park
Description: Gregory Mill Park features a large splash pad open seasonally from May through early September, with extended hours on weekends and weekdays. The 48-acre park combines water play with a playground, .45-mile walking trail, picnic shelters, and grilling facilities, making it a full-service community recreation destination.
Address: 390 Enon Springs Rd E, Smyrna, TN 37167

Name: Coal Creek Park
Description: Coal Creek Park features a seasonal splash pad open from late May through late September with daily operating hours. The facility includes multiple water features served by a 2,700-gallon recirculation system with sand filtration and chemical treatment to maintain water quality. A seasonal café offers refreshments and supplies for splash pad visitors during summer operation.

Name: Williamson County Indoor Sports Complex
Description: Williamson County Indoor Sports Complex includes the Brentwood Splash Park, a dedicated water play area open seasonally during warm months. The splash park operates on its own schedule alongside the facility's other amenities, including an Olympic-size indoor pool and sports courts.

Name: Northwest Family YMCA
Description: This YMCA features a dedicated family splash pad offering water play alongside its other aquatic facilities. The splash pad operates daily with extended hours, providing a designated water-play area for families and young children in the Nashville community.

Name: Franklin Recreation Complex
Description: Franklin Recreation Complex features a dedicated splash park alongside its outdoor pool facility. The splash park operates seasonally with extended hours during summer months, offering water play as a primary recreational attraction at this comprehensive facility.

Name: Martin Luther King Jr. Park
Description: Martin Luther King Jr. Park features a splash pad alongside its inclusive playground, making it a destination for water play and recreation. The park offers various amenities including picnic areas, athletic fields, and trails, providing multiple reasons to visit beyond the water feature.

Name: Fountains at Gateway
Description: Fountains at Gateway features a splash pad on its central plaza, where children can cool off during warm months. The pad operates daily from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m., making it accessible for families visiting the mixed-use development's shops, restaurants, and entertainment venues.

Name: Piney River Resort
Description: Piney River Resort features a newly built pool and splash pad where guests can cool off and enjoy water play. The facility provides swimming and water activities for both children and adults, with additional amenities like dining options available poolside. Located on the Piney River in rural Tennessee near Nashville, the resort combines the splash pad with river-based activities such as kayaking and tubing.
Address: 6869 Piney River Rd N, Bon Aqua, TN 37025

Name: Cedars of Lebanon State Park
Description: Cedars of Lebanon State Park features a dedicated splash pad with multiple fountains and interactive spray elements, including two tipping buckets designed for children. Located on the grounds of this 900-acre state park, the water feature operates seasonally from Memorial Day through Labor Day and is free to use. Visitors can cool off at the splash pad and enjoy nearby shaded picnic areas.

Name: Moore Park Spray Ground
Description: Moore Park Spray Ground is a large interactive water-play area that operates seasonally during summer months. The facility includes picnic amenities and shaded shelters, making it suitable for families to spend extended time. Free parking and public restrooms are available on-site, and leashed dogs are welcome.

Name: Espee Park
Description: Espee Park features a dedicated spray pad designed for cooling off during hot Arizona summers, equipped with a water tower, multiple candy cane-shaped showers, spray rings, and ground-level spray features. The 33-acre park combines this water play area with extensive recreational amenities including a bike park, sports fields, and playground structures, making it a full-service community recreation destination.

Name: Kids Splash Park
Description: Kids Splash Park is a seasonal splash pad located within Kathryn Abbey Hanna Park on Jacksonville's oceanfront, and one of the larger water-play areas in the area. Its spray and misting features help children cool off through the hot North Florida summer, with shaded seating and picnic tables nearby for families. The splash pad runs from the first weekend of May through late October, typically open from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. Access is through Hanna Park's gate, and the surrounding park adds kayak rentals, trails, and beach access to a visit.

Name: Abess Park
Description: Abess Park is a free community park on Jacksonville's east side with a seasonal splash pad that opens for the summer around Memorial Day weekend. The water feature gives families a place to cool off alongside the park's playground, picnic shelter, and shaded seating. Beyond the water play, the park packs a lot into its size — baseball and soccer fields, basketball and tennis courts, and paved trails — and it rarely feels crowded. Open daily from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. with free admission and on-site restrooms.

Name: Wiley Road Playground
Description: Wiley Road Playground is a free neighborhood park on Jacksonville's west side and one of the city's official JaxParks splash pad sites. Reviewers call the splash pad a hidden gem, with water jets that give kids a place to cool off through the North Florida summer. The seasonal water feature opens around Memorial Day weekend and runs into the fall, set within a community park that also offers a playground, picnic shelter, baseball field, pickleball courts, and restrooms. Admission is free for easy drop-in water play.
Hours: Splash pad May–Oct; park daily to 10PM

Name: Murray Hill Playground
Description: Murray Hill Playground is a free community park in Jacksonville's historic Murray Hill neighborhood, and one of the city's JaxParks splash pad sites. The seasonal splash pad opens around Memorial Day weekend, giving kids a place to cool off through the North Florida summer alongside a well-equipped playground. The park packs in plenty beyond the water play - basketball courts, softball and baseball fields, picnic areas, a concession stand, and restrooms - and hosts youth sports leagues through the season. Open daily from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. with free admission.

Name: Pulaski Water Playground
Description: Pulaski Water Playground is a free, seasonal splash facility tucked into Pulaski Park in Chicago's West Town neighborhood. Its centerpiece is a zero-depth pool with an island play structure ringed by interactive water features — spray nozzles that vary in strength and direction, a deck and small staircase, and a fast slide — giving kids a place to cool off all summer. Families appreciate the free admission and the separate areas for younger and older children. Operated by the Chicago Park District, it runs seasonally for family swim; check the park district for current hours and any maintenance closures before visiting.

Name: Altadena Park
Description: Altadena Park is a free City of Phoenix park with a splash pad that gives families a place to cool off through the brutal desert summer. The water feature runs on a seasonal schedule — weekends in the shoulder months, then daily once summer arrives — and the park is ADA accessible with shade structures, a playground, a grill and picnic area, and drinking fountains. Set in the Phoenix valley where summer highs routinely top 100°F, the splash pad and surrounding shade make it a practical spot for cooling off. Admission is free; restroom access can be limited outside scheduled park activity, so plan accordingly.

Name: Nuestro Park
Description: Nuestro Park is a free City of Phoenix park in the south-central part of the city, and one of the city's official splash pad sites. The spray pad runs seasonally — from the last Saturday in May through early October — giving families a place to cool off during the brutal Phoenix summer. The park is well shaded, with a ramada, mature trees, benches, and water fountains, alongside a playground, basketball court, and picnic area. Open daily from 5:30 a.m. to 10 p.m., with the splash pad free to use as part of the public parks system.

Name: Trailside Point Park
Description: Trailside Point Park is a free City of Phoenix splash pad in the Laveen area on the city's southwest side. Its water-play area is loaded with features — ground fountains, a spray gun, and four buckets that dump water on a regular cycle — giving kids plenty to enjoy through the punishing desert summer. The splash pad runs seasonally, with weekend hours in the shoulder months and daily operation once summer arrives. Beyond the water play, the park offers a covered ramada, playground, restrooms, lighted basketball and sand volleyball courts, and a lake. Admission is free as part of the public parks system.

Name: Paiute Park
Description: Paiute Park is a free, 8-acre City of Scottsdale park with a splash pad that runs nearly year-round, thanks to Scottsdale's mild climate — the spray pad operates daily whenever temperatures climb above 70 degrees. The water starts out warm, making it comfortable for young children. Beyond the splash pad, the park packs in a playground, lighted basketball court, reservable lighted soccer fields, a sand volleyball court, two drop-in ramadas for shade, and restrooms. Open daily from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. with free admission as a public park amenity.

Name: Chesnutt Park
Description: Chesnutt Park is a free City of Scottsdale park with a button-operated splash pad — kids press a button to trigger the water, a fun, water-saving touch that keeps the spray going through the desert heat. Like other Scottsdale splash pads, it runs daily whenever temperatures top 70 degrees, giving the park a long season. The park also offers two playgrounds with slides and climbing structures, a shaded play area, a stone climbing feature beside the splash pad, and pickleball and tennis courts. Park hours run from sunrise to 10:30 p.m., with free admission.
Address: 4565 N Granite Reef Rd, Scottsdale, AZ 85251
Hours: Park sunrise–10:30PM; splash pad runs when above 70°F

Name: Highland Kids Playground and Splash Pad
Description: Highland Kids Playground and Splash Pad is a free, community-open water-play spot in north Scottsdale near Pinnacle Peak, operated by Highlands Church and welcoming to all families. The splash pad comes alive in spring and summer with multiple emitters that shoot water more than 12 feet high and a 'kid car wash' ring kids run through. The fully fenced playground is secured by self-closing gates, with plenty of shade, an accessible family restroom with a changing table, and a water bottle fill station. Open daily from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m.; swim diapers are required for children who aren't potty trained.
Address: 9050 E Pinnacle Peak Rd, Scottsdale, AZ 85255

Name: Lettie Kendall Park
Description: Lettie Kendall Park is a free City of Clarksville park with a splash pad that gives families a place to cool off during the hot, humid Middle Tennessee summer. The water-play area features sprays and fountains, running seasonally during the summer months from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. Beyond the splash pad, the park offers playgrounds, a walking trail, and a rentable pavilion, making it an easy spot for a family afternoon. Admission is free as part of the Clarksville Parks and Recreation system.

Name: Dixon Park
Description: Dixon Park is a free City of Clarksville park in downtown, next to the historic L&N Train Station, with a splash pad that helps families beat the humid Middle Tennessee summer. The water-play area runs seasonally from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. The park is laid out with two play areas — one for older kids and one for younger — with a pavilion of benches, tables, and restrooms set between them, plus a basketball court. Admission is free as part of the Clarksville Parks and Recreation system.

Name: Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park
Description: Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park is a free City of Tampa park on the west bank of the Hillsborough River, just across from downtown, with a splash pad that anchors a lively waterfront destination. The water-play area features a big tipping splash bucket, set beside a fenced 'play cove' with playground equipment for kids ages 2 to 12. Beyond the water play, the 23-acre park offers sports courts, open lawns, a boathouse, and downtown skyline views. The splash pad and all park areas are free; hours run roughly 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. in the warm months and shorter in winter.

Name: Ballast Point Park
Description: Ballast Point Park is a free City of Tampa park on the South Tampa waterfront, where Interbay Boulevard meets Hillsborough Bay, with a splash pad that's a neighborhood favorite. The zero-depth water-play area features colorful flower fixtures that spray cool water and ground jets, with shaded benches around the perimeter so parents can watch and stay cool. The splash pad runs seasonally — longer hours in the warm months — and shuts off below 60 degrees or in bad weather. The park also offers a playground, restrooms, and bay views, all free to the public.
